significance: A gurdwara in Khanewal district marking the inn of Sajjan Thug, where Sikh tradition places Guru Nanak's encounter with him; the inn was turned into a shrine to commemorate the meeting. The present building was raised in Samvat 1970 by a descendant of Bhai Jodh Singh.
story: Sajjan is said to have robbed the travellers he sheltered until Guru Nanak sang him a hymn on the worthlessness of a bronze vessel that is bright outside and black within, upon which he confessed and became a follower.
